context.why: This feature is open for the maintainer's review. An earlier change (decisions.md D26, D28) gave each registered sample and measurement type its own heading on the interactive documentation page, replacing the two headings `samples` and `measurements`. The maintainer did not ask for that and wants the two headings back, with everything the registration says about a type kept. He also wants to see the second documentation page (ReDoc) with the types nested under those headings. decisions.md D29 and tasks T075 and T076 in tasks.md Phase 11 record it, and the specification's FR-036 and User Story 5 scenario 5 are already changed to match.
prior_decisions: decisions.md D29 is the instruction; read it, and D28 for how the current per-type sections are built (fairdm/api/schema.py and generate_viewset in fairdm/api/viewsets.py).

T075, the schema at /api/v1/schema/ that the interactive page at /api/v1/docs/ reads: every registered sample type's operations carry exactly one tag, `Samples`, and every measurement type's exactly one, `Measurements`. Projects, datasets and contributors keep their own tags, written with a capital to match (`Projects`, `Datasets`, `Contributors`). The top-level `tags` list describes those five and nothing else: `Samples` and `Measurements` each get one short translatable sentence saying what the heading holds. Each operation of a registered type gets a `summary` of the form `<plural name>: <what it does>` (for example `Rock Samples: list`, `Rock Samples: create`, `Rock Samples: read`, `Rock Samples: replace`, `Rock Samples: change`, `Rock Samples: delete`), the second part translatable, so the operations of one type sit together and can be told apart under the shared heading. Within a heading, the operations of one type must be adjacent and types in the order the registry gives them: check the order drf-spectacular emits (SORT_OPERATIONS is False in SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS) and what the interactive page does with it, and say in the report what you found. Every operation of a type keeps the type's description as its description. The type's LIST operation's description additionally carries, after the description, the authority, citation and keywords and a link to the repository, exactly the details the per-type tag description carries today (reuse that code; an operation has `externalDocs` too, use it for the repository link as the tag did). Never the maintainer's name or email address. The record component's `title` and `description` stay as they are now.

T076, the second page: /api/v1/redoc/ must read a schema of its own, served at a second address under /api/v1/schema/ (for example `v1/schema/nested/`, named in fairdm/api/urls.py beside the existing schema route), produced by drf-spectacular's own per-view settings (SpectacularAPIView.as_view(custom_settings={...}) with one more postprocessing hook after the existing ones) and no other mechanism. That extra hook rewrites the finished schema: each registered type's operations are tagged with the type's plural name in place of `Samples` or `Measurements`; the top-level `tags` gains one entry per type with the type's description and details (as D28 built them) and its repository link as externalDocs; and the vendor extension `x-tagGroups` lists three groups: one holding Projects, Datasets and Contributors (name it for what it holds, translatable), `Samples` holding every sample type's tag, and `Measurements` holding every measurement type's tag. In this schema an operation's summary can drop the type prefix, since its heading already names the type. A sample type and a measurement type with the same plural name must not collide: if two types would get the same tag name, say so in the report and make the tag names distinct in the simplest way. The two schemas must have the same paths, the same components and the same security schemes; a test compares them. The interactive page keeps reading the first schema.

Tests replace tests/test_api/test_schema.py::TestTypesInTheDocumentation and adjust TestMetadataDescriptionComesFirst (which reads a per-type tag: it should read the list operation's description in the first schema, or the per-type tag in the second) and anything in tests/test_api/test_settings.py that pins per-type tags. Name each changed test in progress.md. These edits are authorised. Tests assert on structure and on values taken from the registration and from model names, never on our own sentences.

Documentation: docs/portal-development/restful-api.md, section 'Model Descriptions in the API Docs' and wherever the page describes the two documentation pages: say how types are grouped on each page, which registration metadata appears where, and the second schema's address. Correct this feature's entry in CHANGELOG.md where it says the documentation has a section per type.

Update feature-state.json for T075 and T076 (status, attempts, evidence with tests, commands, code as path:line, verified_by_ci) and tick them in tasks.md. Every `## D<n>` section you add to decisions.md must end with a line `**ADR:** none — <reason>`.
Write your completion report to specs/011-restful-api/report-fix-4.json. Do not run `ruff check` with fixing over the whole tree; lint only the files you touch.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the first schema, then sample types share the Samples tag and measurement types the Measurements tag, no tag is one type's name, each type's operations are titled with its plural name, and its list operation carries the registration's description and details without maintainer details.

Given the second schema, then each type has its own described tag inside a group for its kind, the two schemas have the same paths, components and security schemes, and the second documentation page reads the second schema.
